## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double anonymized. The guide says submissions are first assessed by the editors and, if deemed suitable, typically sent to at least two reviewers; the editors decide. The title page (with author details) and an anonymized manuscript (including references and tables, without acknowledgments) are separate files (https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/teaching-and-teacher-education/publish/guide-for-authors, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Elsevier's Article Transfer Service: the editors may suggest transferring a manuscript to another Elsevier journal, where it is independently reviewed by that journal's editors (same guide, retrieved 2026-11-23). No journal-specific cascade list is given |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. The guide read does not mention publishing reviewer reports (searched the page text for "open peer" and "transparent review"; only unrelated hits) |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Blank. No source found. SciRev shows "n/a" for average review rounds (https://scirev.org/journal/teaching-and-teacher-education/) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. The guide read gives no instruction on suggesting reviewers |
| **Appeals** | One appeal per submission is allowed under Elsevier's appeal policy; the decision is then final (guide, retrieved 2026-11-23) |

## Format

> Source: guide for authors, https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/teaching-and-teacher-education/publish/guide-for-authors, retrieved 2026-11-23, section "Journal specific information: Writing and formatting" unless stated.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Qualitative, quantitative and mixed-method empirical studies and high-quality review studies that evaluate and synthesise existing research (aims page, https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/teaching-and-teacher-education/about/aims-and-scope). The aims page lists types that will not be considered: book reviews; essays or conceptual papers lacking empirical evidence; frameworks or models without empirical support and critical analysis; basic instrument validation; replication studies that do not show originality; policy or practice reports lacking critical and theoretical analysis; local case studies without broader relevance; large-scale surveys not grounded in critical and theoretical analysis; bibliometric or content analyses |
| **Word limit** | 5,000-9,000 words. The count includes abstract and footnotes and excludes references, tables, figures and appendices; the word count goes in the cover letter |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The guide gives the range without stating exceptions |
| **Abstract limit** | At most 150 words, with a content list for empirical articles (context or rationale, question, methods, findings, implications) and for review articles (theory or principles, review method and period, implications); 3 to 6 keywords in English; 3 to 5 highlights of at most 85 characters each, required at submission; graphical abstract encouraged |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap found; references are outside the 5,000-9,000-word count. Style is APA 7th edition, and the cover letter must confirm use of APA |
| **Supplementary material** | Supplementary files can be added or replaced only at the revision stage; the guide also describes optional co-submission of a data or methods article to Data in Brief or MethodsX |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Tables should be used sparingly and not duplicate the text; artwork goes in separate files, with minimum resolution rules given (for example 300 dpi for combination artwork) |
| **Style / submission format** | Word (.doc/.docx, single column) or LaTeX (.tex); PDF is not accepted as a source file; good English in American or British usage but not mixed; CRediT author contributions required from the corresponding author; separate title page and anonymized manuscript |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes, stated by the journal. Submissions must be firmly grounded in current international teaching and teacher education research, show significant originality, have robust theoretical grounding, and take an international perspective or address globally relevant issues; manuscripts not meeting this "will not be forwarded for review" (aims page, https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/teaching-and-teacher-education/about/aims-and-scope, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- **If yes, what kind?** Engagement with the international teacher-education literature and a theoretical contribution, with the teacher and the act of teaching central; themes named on the page include identity, well-being, motivation and professional learning (same page). The aims list nine submission types that will not be considered (see Format).
- **Article type and length**: empirical or review studies of 5,000-9,000 words, abstract at most 150 words, highlights required (https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/teaching-and-teacher-education/publish/guide-for-authors, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- **Scope signals in the data**: OpenAlex topic-assignment counts are led by teacher education and leadership studies (4006), mathematics education (787) and evaluation of teaching practices (738) (see Subject Density); preservice, student-teacher or initial-teacher-education terms appear in 201 of 771 abstracts (26.07%, regex below).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: the aims page says non-conforming manuscripts will not be forwarded for review. SciRev holds 2 reviews, both immediate rejections (27 and 21 days; https://scirev.org/reviews/teaching-and-teacher-education/); one reviewer-supplied rejection letter, paraphrased, says the editors checked the conceptual framework, literature review, methodological clarity, findings and how the study sits within the international research community. n=2, not a rate.

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are articles of this source dated 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23 whose title or abstract matches the regex (Python `re`, case-insensitive unless marked). Denominator: 771 articles with an abstract in OpenAlex of 1877 articles in the window (41.1% coverage), so counts are lower bounds and shares are shares of abstract-bearing articles. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): hits = 0 gives 0; share under 1% gives 1; 1-5% gives 2; over 5% gives 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. Scores measure how often a method appears in abstracts, not how reviewers judge it. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 2 | Experimental or randomized regex 33 (4.28%). Non-experimental quantitative work is more common: `survey` or `questionnaire` 117 (15.18%, would score 3); regression, multilevel or SEM regex 74 (9.60%); `longitudinal` 56 (7.26%). The aims page accepts quantitative studies but excludes large-scale surveys not grounded in critical and theoretical analysis (https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/teaching-and-teacher-education/about/aims-and-scope) |
| Qualitative interviews | 3 | `interview(s\|ed\|ing)?` 200 (25.94%); `qualitative` 120 (15.56%); thematic analysis or grounded theory 37 (4.80%); `case stud(y\|ies)` 55 (7.13%) |
| Autoethnography | 1 | `auto-?ethnograph\w*` 3 (0.39%). Related: narrative inquiry or self-study 10 (1.30%, would score 2); on the board page 5 of 64 entries list self-study among their interests and 2 list autoethnography or auto/duoethnography (case-insensitive text search of the page, https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/teaching-and-teacher-education/about/editorial-board) |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 1 | `philosophical` 3 (0.39%); `conceptual` 22 (2.85%). The aims page excludes essays or conceptual papers that lack empirical evidence, so a low score is consistent with a stated editorial position (aims URL above) |
| Mixed methods | 3 | `mixed[- ]methods?` 59 (7.65%); the aims page names mixed-method studies as accepted |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 1 | `meta-analys[ie]s` 1 (0.13%); `systematic (literature )?review` 3 (0.39%); `scoping review` 17 (2.20%). The aims page accepts high-quality review studies but excludes bibliometric or content analyses |
| Action research / design-based (added row) | 2 | `action research` or `design-based` 14 (1.82%) |
| Ethnography (added row) | 2 | `ethnograph\w*` 8 (1.04%) |

### Voice & Style

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | No explicit ethics-approval or consent rule was found on the guide page read: the page text was searched for ethics, consent, human subjects and participants, and the only ethics content is a link to Elsevier's general publishing-ethics policies plus declarations of interest and funding (https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/teaching-and-teacher-education/publish/guide-for-authors, retrieved 2026-11-23). The linked publisher policy was not read, so a rule may exist there |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers are a minority: 237 of 1936 Crossref records with author lists (12.2%) in 2021-01 to 2026-11-23; 3-author and 4+-author papers together are 1212 (62.6%) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Blank. The title page must give affiliations "where the work was carried out" and the guide states no rule for authors without an institution (guide URL above, retrieved 2026-11-23); no count of independent-scholar authors was made |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Yes. Option C of Elsevier's research data guidelines applies: deposit research data in a relevant repository and give a link at submission, or state why sharing is not possible, which is published with the article (guide URL above, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double anonymized with a separate title page; acknowledgments go only on the title page; identifying information must be removed from the manuscript and supplementary materials (guide URL above, retrieved 2026-11-23). The guide allows preprints and says they do not count as prior publication; it does not say whether a public preprint affects anonymity |
| **AI use** | Declaration required at submission in a section before the references; AI cannot be an author (guide URL above, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Open access and cost** | Subscription route has no author fee; open access carries a USD 3,900 APC before taxes, which may differ by author (https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/teaching-and-teacher-education/about/insights, retrieved 2026-11-23). 778 of 1877 recent articles are hybrid open access in OpenAlex |
| **Authorship and conflicts** | CRediT roles required from the corresponding author; group authorship declared on the title page; editors with an affiliation to the journal must declare it (guide URL above) |

### AI-Research Notes (sources, blanks, and cross-language checks)

**signal_quality (0-5)**: overall 3. Per layer: OpenAlex counts (methods, topics, countries, types) 3 (only 41.1% of articles have an abstract, so shares are lower bounds); Crossref (counts by year, author lists) 3 but 0 of 2024 records carry an abstract; journal-specific policies and guidelines 4 (aims, guide, board, insights and issues pages read directly, 2026-11-23); publisher-wide policies 3; experiential layer 1 (SciRev n=2, immediate rejections only).

**Pages and what they supplied**: aims page (scope, excluded types, international-perspective rule); guide for authors (peer review model, AI, preprints, data, format, word limit, abstract, highlights, ethics links); editorial board (64 entries, recounted); insights page (CiteScore, publishing timeline, acceptance rate, APC, ISSN); issues list (volumes per year); Elsevier sharing and generative-AI policy pages (publisher level).

**Experiential checks**: SciRev journal page and review list (https://scirev.org/journal/teaching-and-teacher-education/ and https://scirev.org/reviews/teaching-and-teacher-education/): 2 reviews, both "Rejected (im.)", decision times 27 and 21 days (the journal page prints a 24-day figure for immediate rejection), no first-review-round, acceptance-time, round-count or report-quality data (all n/a). LetPub (https://www.letpub.com/index.php?page=journalapp&view=search&searchname=Teaching+and+Teacher+Education&searchissn=0742-051X): the search page returned no journal row, so no LetPub data. 小木虫 / 知乎: one web search for the journal name with 投稿 经验 审稿周期 returned only journal-information sites and no muchong or zhihu thread; fabiaoji not reached. Reddit: one web search for the journal name with submission, desk reject and reddit returned no thread. All of these are "0 first-hand reports beyond SciRev n=2".

**Real browser also failed:** https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/teaching-and-teacher-education/open-access was opened in a real browser on 2026-11-24 and ScienceDirect answered "Page not found" (a 404, not a bot block), so the address does not exist; Elsevier's journal-specific embargo lookup was not tried.

**Unreadable pages**: that open-access address (404 in a real browser too); the Wayback route was not needed because the other publisher pages returned 200.

**Fields deliberately left blank, and why**: abbreviation (no page states it), word-limit negotiability, reviewer-report publication, R+R rounds, reviewer suggestion rules, preprint under-review stage, embargo months, independent-scholar rule, desk rejection rate, reviewer competence and quantitative-bias rows (no first-hand source). Impact factor and quartile: paywalled, not stated by policy.

**Method note**: `scripts/import_openalex.py` produced the scaffold. Keyword counts were produced from a paged OpenAlex works pull (200 per page, 11 requests at about 2-second spacing, no key, no 429 received), reconstructing abstracts from OpenAlex's inverted index and applying the regexes listed above locally. Crossref was used only for year counts and author lists because it holds no abstracts for this journal.

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope and originality**: the aims page says manuscripts without an international perspective or global relevance, or lacking substantive originality and theoretical grounding, will not be forwarded for review (Framing Requirements; aims page). A national or regional case with no wider framing falls under this stated rule.
- **Excluded types**: book reviews, conceptual essays without empirical evidence, bibliometric or content analyses, and the other types in Format are stated as not considered (Format; aims page).
- **Length**: 5,000-9,000 words excluding references, tables, figures and appendices (Format; guide).
- **Anonymisation**: a double-anonymized submission needs a separate title page and an anonymized manuscript, with acknowledgments only on the title page (Peer Review; guide).
- **AI use**: undisclosed generative AI use breaches the guide's declaration rule (AI Policy).

### Soft Tax

- **Required extras**: highlights (3-5 bullets of at most 85 characters), a 150-word abstract with a stated content list, APA 7, CRediT roles, a word count and an APA confirmation in the cover letter, and a data-repository link or an explanation (Format, Practical Concerns; guide).
- **Open access cost**: the OA route costs USD 3,900 before taxes unless an institutional agreement applies; the subscription route has no author fee (Open Access; insights page).
- **Time**: the publisher prints 213 days from submission to acceptance and 74 days to a decision after review (Review Cycle Time; insights page); the definition and period of these figures are not printed.
- **Selectivity signal**: the publisher prints an 8% acceptance rate (Metrics; insights page), with no stated period.

### Best Suited For

- Empirical studies of teachers, teaching or teacher education with an international framing and a theoretical contribution: the aims page prioritises these, and in the 771 abstracts interviews appear in 25.94%, surveys in 15.18%, mixed methods in 7.65% and preservice or initial-teacher-education terms in 26.07% (Framing Requirements, Methodological Preferences).
- Teacher well-being, emotion, motivation, identity and professional learning: named in the aims and frequent in the counts (`well-being|burnout|emotion` 19.71%, `professional (development|learning)` 22.57%) (Sensitive Topics, Framing Requirements).
- High-quality reviews of teacher research that address a specific question: the aims accept them, though only 20 of 771 abstracts (2.59%) match review terms (Methodological Preferences).

### Not Recommended For

- Purely conceptual or philosophical essays: the aims page excludes conceptual papers without empirical evidence, and `philosophical` appears in 3 of 771 abstracts (Format, Methodological Preferences).
- Nationally or locally bounded case studies or policy descriptions with no wider theoretical analysis: stated as not considered (Format; aims page).
- Authors who need a short manuscript: the stated range starts at 5,000 words (Format).
- Anyone needing a verified review-time profile from authors' reports: SciRev has 2 reviews, both immediate rejections (Review Cycle Time, AI-Research Notes); the figures that exist are the publisher's unlabelled averages.
